alt: La Laia i l’Ona parlen al taulell de la cuina, amb dues llibretes tancades.
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one single landscape 3:2 illustration, ideally 1536×1024, for a Catalan listening-comprehension worksheet and catalogue card, printed around 80 mm wide. Reference images specify only canonical character appearance and established drawing style. Fine naturalistic ink and softly textured muted watercolor, warm paper fading into a generous pure-white border on all four edges; no frame. Warm gentle light, restrained earthy colors. Single coherent specific scene, large readable figures and natural hands, no panels, no labels, writing, numerals, logos or watermark. Keep all reference character faces, ages and clothing consistent; do not include the lettering or layout of the model sheets. Characters: Laia, young freckled girl with curly chestnut hair in a high bun and a sage-green sweater; Ona, adult dark-skinned woman with braided low bun, cream chef shirt and terracotta apron. In a restaurant kitchen, they lean towards two closed, plain clothbound notebooks lying together on an otherwise empty work counter. Laia is about to ask something and Ona listens with a warm practical expression. Hands natural, covers closed, background reduced to soft cupboards. Do not show writing, cover labels, recipes, numbers, color-coded meaning, ingredients, dishes, cake, baking tins, a phone, a photo, burnt or stuck food, copied sheets or a solved action.
encoding: WebP quality 90; original composition and dimensions retained.

edits.prompt: Edit the supplied image with a single precise object-color change. Preserve the light cream page edges and all the notebook geometry. Keep the LEFT green notebook exactly green. Preserve all other aspects of this illustration unchanged: Laia and Ona's faces, ages, skin, hair, clothes, hand positions, expressions, kitchen, counter, lighting, warm watercolor/ink medium, white vignette border, composition, framing and dimensions. No text or numbers. Do not open either notebook or add any recipes, ingredients, pans or new props. The right notebook must read unambiguously as black, not brown.
